misconceptions.description: Believing a longer, more elaborate prompt is automatically a better-constrained prompt
misconceptions.trigger: teacher adds adjectives and wishes (engaging, rigorous, fun) but no measurable limits the plan must respect
misconceptions.feedback: A strong constraint is checkable: a time cap, a banned tool, a required standard, a reading level. Adjectives are not constraints.

misconceptions.description: Treating a preference (would be nice to include movement) the same as a non-negotiable limit (IEP requires extended time)
misconceptions.trigger: teacher lets the AI trade away a legal or safety requirement to satisfy a stylistic wish
misconceptions.feedback: Separate hard constraints the plan must satisfy from soft preferences. Never let a soft preference override an accommodation or safety rule.

misconceptions.description: Assuming the AI honored a stated constraint without checking the returned plan against it
misconceptions.trigger: teacher states no homework but the plan still assigns reading at home, and the teacher submits it unchecked
misconceptions.feedback: After each prompt, re-read the plan against every hard constraint. A stated constraint is not a satisfied constraint.
